stem: The Earth's interior is made up of how many main layers?
solution: The Earth has three layers: the crust (outermost), the mantle (middle) and the core (innermost).

stem: Which is the outermost layer of the Earth?
solution: The crust is the thin, outermost solid layer on which we live.

stem: The innermost and hottest layer of the Earth is the:
solution: The core is the innermost layer; its inner part is extremely hot and is made mainly of nickel and iron ('nife').

stem: The continental crust is composed mainly of silica and alumina, referred to as:
solution: The continental crust ('sial') is rich in silica (si) and alumina (al); the oceanic crust ('sima') is rich in silica and magnesium.

stem: The central core of the Earth is made up largely of which metals?
solution: The core is composed mainly of nickel (ni) and iron (fe), hence called 'nife'.

stem: Rocks formed from the cooling and solidification of molten magma are called:
solution: Igneous rocks form when hot molten magma/lava cools and hardens (e.g. basalt, granite).

stem: Rocks formed by the accumulation and compression of sediments over long periods are:
solution: Sedimentary rocks (e.g. sandstone) form from layers of sediment that get compacted and cemented over time.

stem: When existing rocks change form under great heat and pressure, the new rocks formed are called:
solution: Metamorphic rocks form when igneous or sedimentary rocks are transformed by intense heat and pressure (e.g. marble from limestone).

stem: The continuous process by which one type of rock changes into another over time is called the:
solution: The rock cycle describes how igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks transform into one another over geological time.

stem: Naturally occurring substances with definite chemical composition, of which rocks are made, are called:
solution: Minerals are naturally occurring substances with a specific chemical composition; rocks are aggregates of one or more minerals.

stem: The middle layer of the Earth, between the crust and the core, is the:
solution: The MANTLE is the MIDDLE layer of the Earth, lying BETWEEN the CRUST and the CORE, and extends to a great depth. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The crust is the thinnest layer of the Earth, being thicker under the:
solution: The CRUST is the THINNEST layer, and it is THICKER under the CONTINENTS (about 35 km) than under the OCEANS (about 5 km). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The molten (semi-liquid) material found below the Earth's crust is called:
solution: The MOLTEN (semi-liquid, very hot) material found BELOW the Earth's crust is called MAGMA; when it flows out onto the surface, it is called lava. So option 1 is correct.

stem: When magma reaches the Earth's surface (e.g. through a volcano), it is called:
solution: When MAGMA reaches the Earth's SURFACE (through a volcano or crack), it is called LAVA, which then cools to form igneous rock. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Igneous rocks are also called 'primary rocks' because they:
options: Were the first rocks to form, from cooling magma
solution: IGNEOUS rocks are called 'PRIMARY ROCKS' because they were the FIRST rocks to FORM, from the COOLING of MAGMA/lava — other rock types later formed from them. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Igneous rocks are classified into intrusive and extrusive types. Extrusive igneous rocks form:
options: When lava cools on the Earth's surface
solution: EXTRUSIVE igneous rocks form when LAVA COOLS on the Earth's SURFACE (e.g., basalt), cooling quickly with small crystals. INTRUSIVE rocks (e.g., granite) form when magma cools slowly deep inside. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Basalt is an example of which type of rock?
solution: BASALT is an example of an IGNEOUS (EXTRUSIVE) rock, formed from lava that cooled on the surface — the Deccan Traps of India are made of basalt. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Granite is an example of which type of rock?
solution: GRANITE is an example of an IGNEOUS (INTRUSIVE) rock, formed when magma cooled SLOWLY deep inside the Earth, producing large crystals. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Crust — outermost 2. Mantle — middle 3. Core — innermost. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE are correct: CRUST → OUTERMOST; MANTLE → MIDDLE; CORE → INNERMOST layer of the Earth. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Sedimentary rocks often contain fossils, which are:
options: The preserved remains or impressions of ancient plants and animals
solution: SEDIMENTARY rocks often contain FOSSILS — the PRESERVED REMAINS or IMPRESSIONS of ANCIENT PLANTS and ANIMALS — because sediments buried them over time. Fossils help us study the past. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly pairs a rock with its type?
options: Sandstone → sedimentary; Marble → metamorphic; Granite → igneous
Sandstone → igneous; Marble → sedimentary; Granite → metamorphic
solution: The correct pairings are: SANDSTONE → SEDIMENTARY; MARBLE → METAMORPHIC (from limestone); GRANITE → IGNEOUS. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Marble, used in monuments like the Taj Mahal, is a metamorphic rock formed from:
solution: MARBLE is a METAMORPHIC rock formed from LIMESTONE (a sedimentary rock) under heat and pressure. It was used in the Taj Mahal and many monuments. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the rock cycle, igneous and sedimentary rocks can become metamorphic rocks through:
solution: In the ROCK CYCLE, IGNEOUS and SEDIMENTARY rocks can become METAMORPHIC rocks through GREAT HEAT and PRESSURE deep in the Earth. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the rock cycle, when rocks melt into magma and then cool, they form:
solution: In the ROCK CYCLE, when rocks MELT into MAGMA and then COOL, they form IGNEOUS ROCKS again — completing the cycle of transformation. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The temperature and pressure inside the Earth generally:
options: Increase as we go deeper toward the core
solution: The TEMPERATURE and PRESSURE inside the Earth generally INCREASE as we go DEEPER toward the CORE, which is extremely hot and under immense pressure. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The Earth's core is very hot. Reason (R): It is the innermost layer, under great pressure and made of nickel and iron. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — the core is very hot. R is TRUE and correctly EXPLAINS A: it is the INNERMOST layer, under GREAT PRESSURE and made of NICKEL and IRON, conditions that make it extremely hot. So R is the correct explanation of A. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The oceanic crust ('sima') is rich in silica and:
solution: The OCEANIC CRUST ('SIMA') is rich in SILICA (si) and MAGNESIUM (ma). The continental crust ('sial') is rich in silica and alumina. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Rocks are useful to humans because they:
options: Provide minerals, building materials and fertile soil (when weathered)
solution: ROCKS are useful because they PROVIDE MINERALS (metals, coal), BUILDING MATERIALS (stone, marble), and, when WEATHERED, form the FERTILE SOIL on which plants grow. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The breaking down of rocks into smaller pieces by weather over time is called:
solution: The BREAKING DOWN of ROCKS into SMALLER PIECES by the WEATHER (heat, cold, water, wind) over time is called WEATHERING — a key step in forming soil and sediments. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Soil is formed over a long time from:
options: The weathering of rocks mixed with organic matter
solution: SOIL is formed over a LONG TIME from the WEATHERING of ROCKS mixed with ORGANIC MATTER (decayed plants and animals) — the thin, life-supporting top layer. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following statements about the Earth's layers is correct?
options: The crust is thin and solid, the mantle is thick and hot, and the core is the hottest and densest
solution: It is correct that the CRUST is THIN and SOLID, the MANTLE is THICK and HOT, and the CORE is the HOTTEST and DENSEST layer of the Earth. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Coal and petroleum are found in which type of rock formation?
solution: COAL and PETROLEUM are found in SEDIMENTARY ROCK formations, having formed from the remains of ancient plants and organisms buried in sediments over millions of years. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a metamorphic rock?
solution: Examples of METAMORPHIC rocks are MARBLE (from LIMESTONE) and SLATE (from clay/shale) — formed under heat and pressure. Basalt and granite are igneous; sandstone is sedimentary. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The study of the Earth's interior is difficult because:
options: We cannot dig very deep, so scientists use indirect evidence like earthquakes and volcanoes
It is easy to reach the core
solution: Studying the Earth's INTERIOR is difficult because we CANNOT DIG very DEEP, so scientists use INDIRECT EVIDENCE like EARTHQUAKE waves and VOLCANIC material to learn about the layers. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is the correct order from the surface to the centre of the Earth?
solution: From the SURFACE to the CENTRE, the correct order is CRUST → MANTLE → CORE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The rock cycle shows that rocks are:
options: Constantly changing from one type to another over long periods
solution: The ROCK CYCLE shows that rocks are CONSTANTLY CHANGING from one type to another (igneous ↔ sedimentary ↔ metamorphic) over LONG PERIODS of time. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why is knowledge of the Earth's interior and rocks important?
options: It helps us find minerals, understand earthquakes and volcanoes, and use resources
solution: Knowledge of the Earth's INTERIOR and ROCKS is important because it helps us FIND MINERALS (for industry), UNDERSTAND EARTHQUAKES and VOLCANOES, and USE the Earth's RESOURCES wisely. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following pairs a layer with its main material correctly?
options: Crust → rocks/soil (sial and sima); Core → nickel and iron (nife)
Crust → nickel and iron; Core → soil
solution: The correct pairing is: CRUST → ROCKS and SOIL (SIAL and SIMA); CORE → NICKEL and IRON (NIFE). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The rocks and minerals of the Earth's crust are the source of most of our:
solution: The ROCKS and MINERALS of the Earth's CRUST are the source of most of our METALS (iron, copper), FUELS (coal, petroleum), and BUILDING MATERIALS (stone, cement) — vital for human life and industry. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The deepest mine or borehole made by humans reaches only a small way into the:
solution: Even the DEEPEST mine or borehole made by humans reaches only a SMALL WAY into the CRUST — we have never reached the mantle or core, which is why we use indirect methods to study them. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best describes a rock?
options: A natural mass made of one or more minerals
solution: A ROCK is a NATURAL MASS made of ONE or MORE MINERALS — the solid material that forms the Earth's crust. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Deccan Plateau of India is largely made of which rock?
solution: The DECCAN PLATEAU of India is largely made of BASALT, an IGNEOUS rock formed from vast ancient lava flows (the Deccan Traps). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following minerals is a source of iron?
solution: IRON ORE (like HAEMATITE and magnetite) is the mineral source of IRON, extracted from certain rocks and used to make steel. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Sediments that form sedimentary rocks are usually deposited by:
solution: The SEDIMENTS that form SEDIMENTARY ROCKS are usually deposited by WATER (rivers, seas), WIND, and ICE (glaciers), which carry and lay down small particles that later harden. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The gradual transformation of rocks in the rock cycle is driven by processes both inside and outside the Earth, such as:
options: Heat and pressure (inside) and weathering and erosion (outside)
solution: The ROCK CYCLE is driven by processes both INSIDE the Earth (HEAT and PRESSURE, melting) and OUTSIDE it (WEATHERING and EROSION by water, wind, and ice). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a rock type with how it forms?
options: Igneous → cooling magma; Sedimentary → compressed sediments; Metamorphic → heat and pressure
Igneous → sediments; Sedimentary → heat; Metamorphic → cooling magma
solution: The correct matches are: IGNEOUS → from COOLING MAGMA; SEDIMENTARY → from COMPRESSED SEDIMENTS; METAMORPHIC → from HEAT and PRESSURE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The crust and the uppermost solid part of the mantle together form the:
solution: The CRUST and the UPPERMOST SOLID PART of the MANTLE together form the LITHOSPHERE — the rigid outer shell of the Earth. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Fossils found in sedimentary rocks are useful because they:
options: Tell us about ancient life and the age of the rocks
solution: FOSSILS in sedimentary rocks are useful because they TELL us about ANCIENT LIFE (extinct plants and animals) and help determine the AGE of the ROCKS — key evidence for studying Earth's history. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about the Earth's structure?
options: It is layered, with each layer differing in material, temperature and state
solution: It is TRUE that the Earth's structure is LAYERED, with EACH LAYER (crust, mantle, core) DIFFERING in MATERIAL, TEMPERATURE, and physical STATE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Inside Our Earth' is that:
options: The Earth's interior cannot be understood

The EARTH has THREE main layers — the thin, solid CRUST (of sial and sima) on which we live, the thick, hot MANTLE below it, and the innermost, hottest CORE (of nickel and iron, 'nife'), with temperature and pressure rising toward the centre; the crust is made of ROCKS, which are aggregates of MINERALS and occur in three types — IGNEOUS (from cooled magma/lava, e.g. granite, basalt), SEDIMENTARY (from compressed sediments, often with fossils, e.g. sandstone) and METAMORPHIC (from heat and pressure, e.g. marble from limestone) — all of which change into one another over long periods through the ROCK CYCLE; these rocks and minerals are the source of soil, metals, fuels and building materials essential to human life
The Earth is made of only one layer
solution: The chapter's overall message is that the EARTH has THREE MAIN LAYERS — the thin, solid CRUST (made of SIAL, rich in silica and alumina, and SIMA, rich in silica and magnesium) on which we live; the thick, hot MANTLE below it; and the innermost, HOTTEST CORE (made mainly of NICKEL and IRON, called 'NIFE') — with TEMPERATURE and PRESSURE rising toward the centre. The crust is made of ROCKS, which are aggregates of MINERALS and occur in THREE TYPES: IGNEOUS rocks (formed from cooled MAGMA/LAVA — e.g., granite and basalt), SEDIMENTARY rocks (formed from compressed SEDIMENTS, often containing FOSSILS — e.g., sandstone, and holding coal and petroleum), and METAMORPHIC rocks (formed under HEAT and PRESSURE — e.g., marble from limestone). Through the ROCK CYCLE, these rocks CHANGE into ONE ANOTHER over LONG PERIODS. These rocks and minerals are the source of SOIL, METALS, FUELS, and BUILDING MATERIALS essential to human life. So the overall message is option 2.
